# Third-party files in baud

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask third-party` from docs/research/third-party.toml,
docs/research/sources/MANIFEST.toml and baud-app/assets/CREDITS.txt. Do not edit:
change the sidecar and regenerate. `cargo xtask sources` fails when this file is stale. -->

baud's own work is under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). This file lists the files in the
tree that are someone else's work or carry some of it, as a licence audit of the tree (2026-10-10)
and a sweep of what scripts/gen-* and scripts/extract-* read and write found them: each file's
licence, where the notice that licence asks for is, and where it came from. Every file in
docs/research/sources/ is listed, and the check fails on one that is not. The licence texts the
files need are beside them or in
[LICENSES/](LICENSES/), and this file lists them; LICENSE is the Creative Commons text alone.
Each crate published to crates.io carries LICENSE, in its own LICENSES/ the texts its
files need, as links to these, and a NOTICE generated from the same rows that names its
third-party files by their paths in the crate, which `cargo xtask publish` checks. Nothing here is legal
advice; where a file's status is a choice still open, this file says so and decides nothing.

## Notices for what the program carries

The notices of every third-party work the `baud` program carries, each with its copyright, what
was changed and its licence, then each licence text once: the same text `baud --credits`
prints, [baud-app/assets/CREDITS.txt](baud-app/assets/CREDITS.txt), which `cargo xtask credits`
writes from the same rows. The rest of this file lists every third-party file in the tree.

```text
Third-party notices for what this build of baud includes.

baud's program file carries the works below. Each notice says what the work
is, where baud uses it, its copyright notices, what was changed, and the
licence text it falls under. The licence texts follow the notices: each text
once, with the copyright notices of every work under it listed above it.

     and Noto Sans Devanagari 2.007

            Tektronix, Inc. All Rights Reserved
            Copyright 1990, 1998 The Open Group
Changes:    Ported to Rust in xcms.rs. baud displays no TekHVC coordinates,
            since a TekHVC colour is read, drawn as sRGB and reported as
            rgb, and calls that colour space TekHVC wherever it names it,
            and uses the term for nothing else.
```

### HarfBuzz 12.3.0's measurements of JetBrains Mono's and Fira Code's variable fonts (advances.txt and marks.txt also measure baud's own gvar, hvar and ink case fonts), the oracle baud-font's variation and mark code is tested against: advances.txt (a glyph's advance at an axis setting, tools/baud-oracle's advance), marks.txt (a mark's offsets and advance after its base, tools/baud-oracle's marks) and normalize.txt (an axis value normalised through avar, tools/baud-oracle's var). Numbers computed from the fonts' metric and positioning tables, not glyph data or a file the fonts' authors released, so OFL condition 5 does not reach them; the fonts themselves are under the OFL beside their licences. The glyph outlines in outlines.txt and cff2-outlines.txt have a row of their own, under the OFL

## docs/research/sources/

Copies of other people's documents and code that baud's research cites, pinned by sha256 in
[MANIFEST.toml](docs/research/sources/MANIFEST.toml). Each group gives the licence, where its
notice is, and the URL each file was copied from.

### vt100.net, 'A parser for DEC's ANSI-compatible video terminals' (Paul Flo Williams). Its RDF names CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, and it sits in the inline SVG's metadata with dc:type StillImage and the diagram's title, so it describes the state diagram. The footer naming CC BY 4.0 is inside an HTML comment in this copy, and vt100.net's emulation index carries a copyright line and no licence (manifest `vt100-net-emu-index`). The same footer was visible on 2023-09-06 and 2023-09-24 over an article line for line this copy's (manifest `williams-dec-ansi-parser-20230906` and `williams-dec-ansi-parser-20230924`), and CC BY 4.0 calls its grant irrevocable (2(a)(1)) and says stopping distribution does not end it (6(c); `cc-by-4-0-legalcode`). The whole file is kept under the stricter BY-NC-SA 3.0.

- **Status:** nc -- kept verbatim under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, which allows a verbatim copy that carries its attribution and the licence's URI; its NonCommercial term binds every copy of this file, whatever the repository's licence
- **Licence:** CC-BY-NC-SA-3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/3.0/)
- **Notice:** the licence's URI, below
